pr_body:
#### What is it? - [ ] Bugfix (user facing) - [x] Feature (user facing) - [ ] Codebase improvement (dev facing) - [ ] Meta improvement to the project (dev facing) #### Description of the changes in your PR The most basic implementation of comment replies. The replies are shown in a fragment opened from the main activity, instead of on top of the video detail fragment. Although this might be a bit unexpected, this can be improved later, since I tried and found it too cumbersome to open fragments on top of each other*. \* *Yet another broken thing in the current app architecture: opening new fragments from within one fragment. With the old Android APIs it would take something like 100 lines of code spread across many files, since you would have to create a stack of fragments in the base activity, then implement proper state saving in the stack, then push and pop items from the stack in the correct way, ... If we used the modern APIs instead, after the initial setup in the topmost activity, it would be as simple as writing something along the lines of `findNavController(...).navigate(viewId, arguments)`.* #### Implementation notes - I removed the comment mini variant since it was never used. Now only one variant exists, which reduced code duplication and made it simpler to edit the layout to add the replies button. - The comment item layout had a few changes (other than adding the replies button) that fixed RTL warnings. - I moved `RelatedItemsInfo` in the same folder as `RelatedItemsFragment`, since it wouldn't make sense for that class to stay in `util`. I also simplified the code in that class. Although this is an unrelated change, I did it because I also added `CommentRepliesInfo` that works in a similar way, and put it in the same folder as `CommentRepliesFragment`. - At first I though that to load comment replies the extractor needed the original `CommentsInfo` object, so I made bb01da3691ff1d5c3dccd41b7ca1a5deb1b5676f, but then I found out that the url is enough, so I reverted that change in 50a3ae67d21538f70c91d26cebc28156f0ea2c10. - The replies page has at the top the starting comment of which replies are shown. The text size there is a bit larger than for comment items, and the comment content is always expanded. - The only code smell reported by Sonar is about `CommentInfoItemHolder.updateFromItem`, but I would ignore this warning since I already simplified many parts of that method in 8bd42d952e52d98a4e33c8046fab5a200f5a5130 and added comments to separate the various actions being performed. #### Before/After Screenshots/Screen Record
Before Video details page Replies page With heart and pin
Note to blog post writers: I just noticed these images contain some aggressive comments in Italian, so they need to be taken again #### Fixes the following issue(s) - Closes #2277 - Fixes #10012 thanks to https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/commit/e236d370c85cbc9766fbd64330d6cf5754fee81d, also see https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipeExtractor/pull/1049 #### APK testing The APK can be found by going to the "Checks" tab below the title. On the left pane, click on "CI", scroll down to "artifacts" and click "app" to download the zip file which contains the debug APK of this PR. This PeerTube video has nested replies, but they don't seem to work: https://share.tube/w/vxu4uTstUBAUromWwXGHrq. #### Due diligence - [x] I read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/blob/HEAD/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). ---- **Notes for the website team:** make sure to modify the [corresponding FAQ entry](https://newpipe.net/FAQ/#bugs-read-comments) when updating the page for the release.

I changed back the title to generalize again this issue because the UI needs to support multiple comment levels. It would be probably not worth it to implement a first temporary UI to support YouTube replies and then a second and general UI for YouTube and PeerTube, which can have multi-level threads, unless someone is able to do so. Extractor changes should probably need to be done first to be able to support multi-thread comments properly. In order to not have waterfall issues (I mean at a certain thread count a very small space for the comment itself), I think using the following structure is the best option we have (that's what YouTube partially use in their mobile app too): Where: - in green: a back button; - in blue: a title such as `Replies` or `Comment replies`; - in yellow (maybe): the comment which has its replies shown below; - in red: comment replies (which can have replies too, which may be the case on PeerTube). Note that I don't know if this programmatically doable, I have no real knowledge in Android development. Help is wanted for this feature.
